claims.text: Epēshu is NOT drawn by genCityCanvas in the shipped site. meshedWorldInit registers it as a canon overlay (art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg, 2863x3072, prov 'canon', 19 POIs), ensureCityGen only generates when there is no registration or prov is 'invented', and ensureCityGenNow returns when CITYREG[key] exists. claims.text: Arterials on the chart: there is no ocher or distinct arterial colour. Every street, avenue and plaza is the same cream as the ground. Width is the only hierarchy: cream-channel ridge widths in Q1 have p25/p50/p75/p90/p99 of 4/4.5/6/8/16 px, and the Forum avenue east of the Forum measures 5-10 px against 4-6 px for ordinary lanes (about 2x). The one differentiated line is a slate-grey (about rgb 95,97,90) wall with square gate-towers: a single arc entering Q1 at its north edge near chart x1570, running south-east then south-west and west along chart y about 3250 to the west edge; Outwall (POI 11, 2047,1386) lies east of it and the Black Barghest Inn (POI 14) beside it.

claims.text: Park voids on the chart are few and small. Three deliberate green spots: the Māmban (POI 8 at 969,2207), a roughly 150 px dark-green canopy mass around a light-green lawn (about rgb 196,207,156) with the badge on top of its core; the Necropolis of the Founders (POI 1), a small tree stand, lawn and a dark stone building on the shore spit; and the Temple of Thobrauk precinct (POI 5), a lawn patch with a dark building at the north edge. Mid-green tree canopy is 12.1% of land in 525 clusters of at least 40 px (largest 29,305 px, the forest wall at the east edge, which continues past Q1); cream open voids at least 25 px across number 37 and cover 9.3% of land, the biggest (142,706 px) being the empty outskirt parcels north-east of the wall, not a park. The sage gridded field with parcel lines (about 330x240 px at chart x1850-2180, y2454-2694) is the only agricultural patch.

claims.text: The DEM coast does not follow the chart coast in the southern half of Q1. Where the DEM first reaches h>=0 east of the sea, it sits 1.0 and 0.8 atlas px (about 78 and 67 chart px) from the chart coast at chart y 1500 and 1800, but 3.8, 7.0, 10.3 and 10.4 atlas px (309, 562, 828, 837 chart px) east of it at y 2100, 2400, 2700 and 3000. DEM land is 58% of Q1 against about 80% on the chart. The northern agreement is within one DEM cell (1.04 atlas px), so the transform looks right and the gap is in the DEM's own sea/land line; relief laid over the chart would drown the south-west quarter unless it is clipped to the chart coast.

claims.text: Against the brief's five Azlen classes, Q1 stands: block grain - chart has it densely (13.7k fills) and the generator thinly; park void - chart has 3 small deliberate green spots and tree masses, generator has none; arterial - chart has width tiers only in cream plus a slate wall, generator has four cream tiers and a brown wall, neither has ocher; fog wash - absent in chart, generator, sim and site (only the parchment tone wash exists); contour hill - absent from the chart and the generator, with only a DEM slope (-20 to 85 m) that disagrees with the chart coast in the south. So for Q1 the chart is the density benchmark and nothing yet supplies the painted classes beyond block grain.

evidence.ref: docs/research/filigree-for-the-table.pdf p4 (painted city: cream sheet, rose-brown block grain, green park voids, contour hair, ocher arterials, watercolor water, fog washes, no chrome, no pins); p5 (Research: 'block, park void, arterial, fog wash, contour hill'); claims q08-c03 to q08-c20

gaps: No vector source exists for the chart's blocks, lawns, wall or streets; every chart figure here is a pixel-colour classification of JPEG tiles. Fill counts (13,669) merge touching blocks and miss tiny ones, so treat them as an order of magnitude, and the 6x and 25x density ratios as approximate.

Which cream avenue is the Road That Walks with the Sun inside Q1 is not established: POI 15 is outside Q1 and the chart labels no street. The Forum avenue width (5-10 px) is a sample at five columns, not a surveyed arterial network.
The wall's length, tower and gate count were not measured (a colour-opening attempt fragmented the line), and nothing in the data says the chart's arc is the wiki's 'crumbling inner wall'.

The wiki's 'hills to the north' are not located inside Q1, and the south-west DEM versus chart coast gap (up to 10.4 atlas px) was measured but not explained (DEM carving versus the chart's drawn coast).
The fog source is undecided: the sim has no fog state, so a fog wash needs a seeded function of place and snapshot day or a new weather state; nothing here chooses.

The generator was forced in headless Chromium with Leaflet served from a local copy (unpkg.com is blocked by the proxy) and Google Fonts aborted, so the cartouche font and anything network-dependent were not exercised; cityApproaches (source of the 3 stubs and approach gates) was not read.

Whether the canon world-zoom overlay maps-site/art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg and the z3 tile chart are the same art was not settled: composition, numbering and the 0.7315 scale match, but a resized Q1 differs from the overlay crop by a mean absolute RGB difference of 13.6, so which one Job 3 should treat as the benchmark is open.
The target colours for rose-brown blocks and ocher arterials are not specified anywhere in the repo, so whether the chart's tan-ochre fill counts as rose-brown is a judgement left to Job 2.
Whether the baked badges and the 19 .poi-mk roundels coincide exactly at deeper zoom than 9.38 was not checked.
summary: Q1 (chart px 2048 square, 0.63 of a hex, 84% inside fixture F10) is a dense block-grain painting with flat water, a slate wall, 12 baked pins and only three small green park spots, and it has no relief, ocher arterials or fog; the DEM supplies one eastward slope (-20 to 85 m) that disagrees with the chart coast in the south. genCityCanvas is never run for Epēshu (the canon overlay shadows it) and, when forced, draws about a sixth of the chart's fill density per image px with no park, hill or fog primitive and baked cartouche chrome. The chart is therefore the density benchmark for Q1 and only block grain has any source; park voids, arterials, fog and contour hills are all gaps.
